title: Equivariant prefix homotopy with finite integral evaluations
statement:
Let $G$ be a topological group, $H\subseteq G$ a subgroup, and $n\geq0$. For $q\geq0$ put $B_q(G)=\mathbf Z[G^{q+1}]$, the free abelian group on ordered tuples with repetitions [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and put $B_{-1}(G)=\mathbf Z[\{()\}]\cong\mathbf Z$, free on the single empty tuple $[\varnothing]$. Put $B_q(G)=0$ for $q<-1$, with zero boundary and zero prefix maps out of these groups. Give these groups the alternating-deletion boundary $\partial$, including $\partial[x]=[\varnothing]$ and $\partial[\varnothing]=0$. Left translation acts on every coordinate and fixes the empty tuple. Suppose homomorphisms $A_q:B_q(G)\to B_q(G)$ are given for $-1\leq q\leq n$, with $A_{-1}=1$, $\partial A_q=A_{q-1}\partial$ for $0\leq q\leq n$, and $A_q(hz)=hA_q(z)$ for $h\in H$. Suppose for every $q\geq0$ in this range there are a finite index set $I_q$, integers $k_{qj}$ and continuous maps $b_{qj}:G^{q+1}\to G^{q+1}$ such that
$$A_q[x]=\sum_{j\in I_q}k_{qj}[b_{qj}(x)].$$
For $b\in G$, let $C_b:B_q(G)\to B_{q+1}(G)$ prefix $b$ to every basis tuple, with $C_b[\varnothing]=[b]$. Set $Q_{-1}=0$ and define $Q_q:B_q(G)\to B_{q+1}(G)$ on basis tuples and then by linear extension, for $0\leq q\leq n$, by
$$Z_q(x)=[x]-A_q[x]-Q_{q-1}(\partial[x]),\qquad Q_q[x]=C_{x_0}Z_q(x).$$
Then $\partial^2=0$, $\partial C_b+C_b\partial=1$ in every degree $q\geq-1$, and $hC_bz=C_{hb}(hz)$. The recursively defined maps satisfy $\partial Z_q(x)=0$ and
$$1-A_q=\partial Q_q+Q_{q-1}\partial\quad(0\leq q\leq n),\qquad Q_q(hz)=hQ_q(z)\quad(h\in H).$$
For each $0\leq q\leq n$ there are a fixed finite list of integers $t_{qj}$ and continuous maps $v_{qj}:G^{q+1}\to G^{q+2}$ such that $Q_q[x]=\sum_jt_{qj}[v_{qj}(x)]$. The formulas can be chosen using only subtuple selection, the given maps $b_{pj}$ and prefixing an input coordinate; coefficient lists require no equality tests on input values. If every coordinate of every $b_{pj}(y)$ is either $y_k$ or $\rho(y_k)a_i$, for fixed continuous $\rho:G\to H$ and fixed $a_i\in G$, the same coordinate description holds for every $v_{qj}(x)$. These formulas are integral and independent of any eventual coefficient group or coefficient topology.

proof.text: In the specified free abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-free-module], a basis assignment $[x]\mapsto w_x$ extends uniquely by $\sum_xm_x[x]\mapsto\sum_xm_xw_x$; this is additive because each chain has a unique finite coefficient expansion. Consequently each $Q_q$ is a well-defined homomorphism once $Q_{q-1}$ has been defined. The prefix point $x_0$ is chosen separately on each basis tuple, before this extension; it is not a choice of a first coordinate for an arbitrary chain.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-set-complex-contractible] to $A=\mathbf Z$, $S=G$, identifying its augmentation target $\mathbf Z$ with $B_{-1}(G)$ by $1\mapsto[\varnothing]$. Its boundary and prefix maps are exactly the displayed ones on every basis tuple. Its statement gives $\partial^2=0$ and the contracting identity $\partial C_b+C_b\partial=1$ for every $b\in G$, including the augmentation degree. Explicitly, $\partial[b,y_0,\ldots,y_q]=[y_0,\ldots,y_q]-C_b\partial[y_0,\ldots,y_q]$, while $\partial C_b[\varnothing]=\partial[b]=[\varnothing]$ and $C_b\partial[\varnothing]=0$.

source.place: Tag 03AT, lemma-homology-complex, last paragraph of the proof: augmented free tuple complex and insertion homotopy.

proof.text: Coordinate deletion commutes with diagonal left translation, so $\partial(hz)=h\partial z$. Also $h[b,y_0,\ldots,y_q]=[hb,hy_0,\ldots,hy_q]$, giving $hC_bz=C_{hb}(hz)$ by linear extension. In degree $-1$ this reads $h[b]=[hb]$, since translation fixes $[\varnothing]$; all maps out of degree $-2$ are zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text: Put $D_q=1-A_q$ for $-1\leq q\leq n$. Then $D_{-1}=0$ and $\partial D_q=D_{q-1}\partial$ for $0\leq q\leq n$. We induct on $q$ to prove both $\partial Z_q(x)=0$ for every basis tuple and $D_q=\partial Q_q+Q_{q-1}\partial$ on all chains. For $q=0$, $Q_{-1}=0$ implies $Z_0(x)=D_0[x]$, hence $\partial Z_0(x)=D_{-1}\partial[x]=0$. By step 2, $\partial Q_0[x]=\partial C_{x_0}Z_0(x)=Z_0(x)$, proving the homomorphism identity in degree zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text:
For $1\leq q\leq n$ assume the identity in degree $q-1$. Applying it to $\partial[x]$ and using step 2 gives
$$\partial Z_q(x)=D_{q-1}\partial[x]-\partial Q_{q-1}\partial[x]=(D_{q-1}-\partial Q_{q-1})\partial[x]=Q_{q-2}\partial^2[x]=0.$$
For $q=1$ the last term uses $Q_{-1}=0$, not an undefined $Q_{-2}$. Thus the recursive correction is a cycle in every required degree.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text:
Using that cycle, step 2 gives
$$\partial Q_q[x]=\partial C_{x_0}Z_q(x)=Z_q(x)-C_{x_0}\partial Z_q(x)=[x]-A_q[x]-Q_{q-1}\partial[x].$$
All maps in this identity are homomorphisms, so checking basis elements proves $1-A_q=\partial Q_q+Q_{q-1}\partial$ on every chain. This completes the induction. No map $A_{n+1}$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text: For equivariance induct from the equivariant zero map $Q_{-1}$. If $Q_{q-1}$ is $H$-equivariant, then the hypothesis on $A_q$ and step 3 imply $Z_q(hx)=hZ_q(x)$, since the boundary of the translated basis tuple is the translate of its boundary. The first coordinate of $hx$ is $hx_0$. Therefore step 3 gives $Q_q[hx]=C_{hx_0}(hZ_q(x))=hC_{x_0}Z_q(x)=hQ_q[x]$. Linear extension proves this for every $z\in B_q(G)$ and $h\in H$, including degree zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text: Construct finite lists by induction, retaining repetitions. For $q=0$, the list for $Q_0[x_0]$ consists of $[x_0,x_0]$ with coefficient $1$ and $[x_0,b_{0j}(x_0)]$ with coefficients $-k_{0j}$; prefixing a tuple here means concatenating its entries. This evaluates to $C_{x_0}([x_0]-A_0[x_0])$, the required basis value. There is no contribution from $Q_{-1}$. Its list length and coefficients are fixed before $x_0$ is supplied.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text: For $q\geq1$, let $\delta_s:G^{q+1}\to G^q$ delete position $s$, $0\leq s\leq q$. If the list for $Q_{q-1}[y]$ is $\sum_jt_{q-1,j}[v_{q-1,j}(y)]$, define the list for $Q_q[x]$ by concatenating: the tuple $(x_0,x)$ with coefficient $1$; the tuples $(x_0,b_{qj}(x))$ with coefficients $-k_{qj}$; and, for each $s,j$, the tuples $(x_0,v_{q-1,j}(\delta_s x))$ with coefficients $-(-1)^s t_{q-1,j}$. Expanding the boundary and the definition of $Q_q$ gives precisely this equality in $B_{q+1}(G)$. This finite concatenation establishes the induction and uses only subtuple selection, the given $b_{pj}$, and prefixing input coordinates. Coefficients are multiplied only by $1$ or $-1$ at this step; equal evaluated tuples are never identified to define a list.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text: All maps in these lists are continuous. A coordinate projection is continuous for the product topology, so each deletion $\delta_s$ is continuous. The base-case maps $x_0\mapsto(x_0,x_0)$ and $x_0\mapsto(x_0,b_{0j}(x_0))$ have continuous coordinates. Inductively, $v_{q-1,j}\circ\delta_s$ is continuous as a composition, and adjoining the continuous coordinate $x_0$ preserves continuity: inverse images of basic product opens are finite intersections of open inverse images of the coordinates. The same argument applies to $(x_0,b_{qj}(x))$. This proves the asserted continuity with no topology placed on the free abelian groups.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent auxiliary expansion below scalar tame-kernel descent: explicit prefix-recursion calculation (not asserted in the blueprint text).

proof.text: For the additional coordinate assertion, induct on these same uncollected lists. Their base coordinates are $x_0$ and the given coordinates of $b_{0j}$, of the stated forms. Under deletion $\delta_s$, the input coordinate $y_k$ becomes $x_{\iota_s(k)}$, where $\iota_s(k)=k$ for $k<s$ and $k+1$ otherwise. Thus $y_k$ and $\rho(y_k)a_i$ become respectively $x_{\iota_s(k)}$ and $\rho(x_{\iota_s(k)})a_i$. Prefixing adds only $x_0$; the given $b_{qj}$ already satisfy the condition. This proves the coordinate assertion. All lists and their coefficients were constructed over $\mathbf Z$ from the fixed lists for $A$; no coefficient group or coefficient topology enters any step, proving the final independence clause.
